lots.title: Standard Print
lots.description: Printing and delivery of standard-run materials on SRA1/B1, SRA2/B2 or SRA3/B3 sheet-fed litho or digital presses. Typical products include A4/A5/99x210mm brochures, leaflets and flyers; A1-A4 posters; oversize pocket folders; NCR pads, forms, headed paper, compliment slips, business cards, envelopes, receipt books; council meeting papers, agendas and reports. Statutory same-day or 24-hour turnaround jobs are scored in part on supplier proximity and delivery speed.
requirements: Print on SRA1/B1, SRA2/B2 or SRA3/B3 sheet-fed litho presses or digital presses.
Products must meet the mandatory minimum Government Buying Standards for paper and paper products (GBS).

Where printed materials are subject to statutory timing (same-day or 24-hour turnaround), selection criteria for specific call-offs will include the supplier's proximity to the buying authority and speed of delivery service offered.

lots.title: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery – Standard & Security Printing/Confidential Print
lots.description: Secure and confidential printing for the Council and its partners — payroll outputs, P60s, pension payslips and statements, confidential service/investigation reports, commercial services contracts, planning surveyors' reports, democratic/cabinet/audit reports, and mail merges such as school admissions letters. Suppliers must be ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 certified, production must be on-premises without third parties, Council staff must be allowed on-premises for checking/verification, and suppliers must maintain annually-tested BC & DR policies. Statutory same-day/24-hour turnaround jobs apply.
requirements: All production must be completed on-premises within the company; no third-party involvement is permitted.
Facilities must be provided for DCC employees to be on company premises during production for checking and verification.
Supplier must hold ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 certification.
Supplier must have its own Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery policies, annually tested.

Where printed materials are subject to statutory timing (same-day or 24-hour turnaround), call-off selection criteria include supplier proximity to the buying authority and speed of delivery service offered.

warnings.message: Appendix A describes the scope and supplier mandatories for each lot but does not enumerate per-lot MEAT / price-quality award weightings. Those are evaluated at each DPS Stage-2 call-off (separate further-competition documents); only generic 'selection criteria will include proximity and delivery speed' is asserted for statutory-turnaround work in Lots 1 and 7.

All per-lot product requirement seeds are derived from explicit 'Examples include (but not limited to)' lists. Lot scope is intentionally broader than the examples, so downstream matching must treat these seeds as representative, not exhaustive.
Specification gives only one aggregate estimate (£140,000 annually on print for the Local Authority); no per-lot monetary estimate is provided in this document.

Source document is a .doc / .docx converted to Docling markdown; page_count is 0 and the markdown contains no page markers. All evidence anchors use section_ref against the document's Part/Lot structure rather than page numbers.

Appendix A does not assign CPV codes to individual lots. The CPV codes attached to each lot output (22000000-0 Printed matter and related products, 79800000-2 Printing and related services) are inherited from the process-level CPV signal and then filtered per lot by whether the lot covers printed products (22000000-0) and/or printing services (79800000-2). Lots 3/4/6/9/10 are tagged 79800000-2 only because they are pure service lots.

The notice already has a single umbrella lot row describing the DPS as a whole (see notice_lots lot-1 description referencing Appendix B Instructions to Bidders). This extraction output supplies the 10 constituent lots referenced there; downstream persistence must replace or supersede the umbrella row with these 10 lots under a single atomic commit cohort for this stage_run.

Parts 2-10 (Packaging, Service Delivery, Complaints, Invoicing, Contract Management, Performance, Innovation, Insurance) are cross-lot DPS-wide obligations. They are not duplicated onto each per-lot 'requirements' array to avoid noisy downstream matching; downstream consumers should treat these as process-level rather than lot-level constraints. Insurance minimums (£5m employers' liability, £5m public liability) are DPS-wide.
